subject: Chemistry
title: Sandmeyer Reaction: Diazonium Salt to Haloarene, Mechanism
summary: An aromatic amine is first turned into a diazonium salt; the diazonium group is then replaced by Cl, Br or I. The halogen goes exactly where the NH₂ group was. In this lesson: aniline is diazotised with NaNO2 and HCl at 273–278 K; the diazonium group is then replaced by Cl (Cu2Cl2/HCl), Br (Cu2Br2/HBr) or I (KI, no copper). Mechanism step by step: Cu+ gives one electron (fishhook arrow), N2 leaves to give the aryl radical, and the radical takes Cl from CuCl2, regenerating Cu+. Key points and two solved questions.

notes.title: Sandmeyer Reaction
notes.blurb: the reaction, why it works, mechanism (fishhook arrows: one electron each), key points

keyPoints: **Sandmeyer**: **N₂ gas** leaves: the driving force. X goes **exactly** where NH₂ was.
**Mechanism · 1–2**: **Fishhook** arrows: one electron each. Ar• = **aryl radical**.

list: **Sandmeyer:** C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ —Cu₂Cl₂ / HCl→ C₆H₅Cl + N₂↑ · C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ —Cu₂Br₂ / HBr→ C₆H₅Br + N₂↑
**Iodide:** C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ + KI → C₆H₅I + KCl + N₂↑ (no copper needed)

blocks.p: The diazonium group is an excellent **leaving group**: it leaves as N₂ gas, which escapes, so the reaction goes to completion. Cu(I) of the cuprous halide gives **one electron** to the diazonium ion and later delivers the halogen; the reaction therefore runs through **radicals**.

head: Step
What happens
rows: ArN₂⁺ + Cu⁺ → Ar–N=N• + Cu²⁺ (Cu⁺ gives one electron; the ion becomes a neutral radical).
Ar–N=N• → Ar• + N₂↑. The C–N bond breaks homolytically: one electron stays on carbon (the **aryl radical**), the other forms the N≡N bond.
Ar• + CuCl₂ → ArCl + CuCl. A new C–Cl bond forms and Cu⁺ is regenerated.

list: ✗ Writing Cu₂I₂ for iodobenzene: KI alone is enough.
✗ Moving the halogen to another position: it replaces NH₂ in place.

blocks.p: **Q1.** Aniline → iodobenzene: C₆H₅NH₂ —NaNO₂, HCl, 273–278 K→ C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ —KI→ C₆H₅I + N₂ + KCl.

simulation.reason: The idea is a fixed sequence of steps drawn in the video and the notes; there is no continuous variable for a student to explore.
